name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - run: uv sync --locked --extra test
      - run: uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files

  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.13", "3.14"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: uv sync --locked --extra test
      - run: uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit

  # Installs the lower bound of each direct dependency in pyproject.toml, so a
  # bound that the code does not work with fails here.
  unit-lowest:
    name: unit (lowest deps)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.10"
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          python-version: "3.10"
      - run: uv venv && uv pip install --resolution lowest-direct -e ".[test]"
      - run: uv pip freeze
      - run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit

  # A push to main runs no acceptance suite: the pull request ran both, and
  # release.yml runs both on the tagged commit.
  acceptance:
    if: github.event_name != 'push'
    # packages: read is for the private images of the cluster setup.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/acceptance-suites.yml

"""The links of README.md, which PyPI shows as the project description. PyPI resolves a relative link against pypi.org, so every link is an absolute URL or an anchor of the page. """ import re from pathlib import Path from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit REPOSITORY = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] README = REPOSITORY / "README.md" FENCED_BLOCK = re.compile(r"^(```|~~~).*?^\1[^\n]*$", re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL) INLINE_CODE = re.compile(r"`[^`\n]*`") # The target of [text](target), ![alt](target) and [text](target "title"). INLINE_LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(\s*]+)>?(?:\s+[\"'(][^)]*)?\)") # A reference definition: [label]: target REFERENCE = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}\[[^\]\n]+\]:\s*]+)", re.MULTILINE) HTML_ATTRIBUTE = re.compile(r"\b(?:href|src)\s*=\s*[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']", re.IGNORECASE) # Both forms name a file of the default branch: ///blob/main/ # on github.com and ///main/ on raw.githubusercontent.com. FILE_ON_MAIN = { "github.com": "/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/", "raw.githubusercontent.com": "/weaviate/to-weaviate/main/", } def link_targets(markdown: str) -> list[str]: # Code is removed first: the text inside it is not a link. The link text # of [`code`](target) is removed with it, the target stays. prose = INLINE_CODE.sub("``", FENCED_BLOCK.sub("", markdown)) return [ target for pattern in (INLINE_LINK, REFERENCE, HTML_ATTRIBUTE) for target in pattern.findall(prose) ] def readme_targets() -> list[str]: return link_targets(README.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) def repository_path(target: str) -> str | None: url = urlsplit(target) prefix = FILE_ON_MAIN.get(url.netloc) if prefix is None or not url.path.startswith(prefix): return None return unquote(url.path[len(prefix) :]) def test_link_targets_finds_every_form_of_link() -> None: markdown = "\n".join( [ "[![badge](https://img.example/b.svg)](LICENSE)", '![alt (with brackets)](docs/demo.gif "title")', "[`docs/seed.py`](docs/seed.py) and [anchor](#install)", "[label]: docs/reference.md", '', "`[not a link](in-code.md)`", "```bash", "echo '[not a link](in-fence.md)'", "```", ] ) assert sorted(link_targets(markdown)) == [ "#install", "LICENSE", "docs/demo.gif", "docs/html.md", "docs/html.png", "docs/reference.md", "docs/seed.py", "https://img.example/b.svg", ] def test_the_readme_has_links() -> None: assert len(readme_targets()) >= 20 def test_every_readme_link_is_absolute_or_an_anchor() -> None: relative = [ target for target in readme_targets() if not target.startswith(("https://", "#")) ] assert relative == [], ( "These README.md links are neither https:// URLs nor #anchors. PyPI " "shows README.md and resolves a relative link against pypi.org. Write " "a link to a file of the repository as " "https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/. Write any " "other link as an https:// URL." ) def test_every_readme_link_to_a_file_on_main_names_a_file_of_the_repository() -> None: paths = [path for target in readme_targets() if (path := repository_path(target))] missing = [path for path in paths if not (REPOSITORY / path).is_file()] assert paths, "README.md links to no file of the repository" assert missing == []

services:

      # Chroma here has no authentication, so only this machine reaches it.

# Development

These pages are for people who change `to-weaviate`. Start with
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) to set up the repository.

| Page | Contents |
|---|---|
| [Architecture](architecture.md) | The layers, the modules, how each command runs through the code, the `Source` protocol |
| [Adding a source](adding-a-source.md) | The files and steps for a new source database |
| [Testing](testing.md) | Test levels, what the tests cover, how to run them, CI |
| [Releasing](releasing.md) | How a version reaches GitHub Releases and PyPI |

The implementation details of each source are in the Implementation section
of its guide, for example [Chroma](../sources/chroma.md#implementation).

# Sources

`to-weaviate` reads from one source per migration. Each source has its own
`inspect` command and its own guide. After `inspect`, the commands are the
same for every source: see [Commands](../commands.md).

| Source | Deployments | Inspect command | Acceptance tests | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chroma | Chroma Cloud, distributed Chroma, single-node Chroma, a Chroma directory on disk | `inspect chroma` | yes | [chroma.md](chroma.md) |

To ask for another source, [open an issue](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/issues/new).
To add one, follow [Adding a source](../development/adding-a-source.md).

## What each guide covers

Every source guide starts from [`_template.md`](_template.md) and has at
least these sections:

1. **Deployments**: which servers and services of the source the tool reads.
2. **Connection settings**: the environment variables of the source.
3. **`inspect <source>` options**: the options that select what to read.
4. **Examples**: the settings and commands for each deployment.
5. **How the data maps to Weaviate**: ids, vectors, text, metadata, distances
   and embedding models.
6. **Writes during a copy**: whether the application can keep writing to
   the source while `copy` and `sync` run.
7. **Limits**: what the tool does not migrate, and source behavior that
   affects a copy.
8. **Implementation**: for developers. The modules, how the source reads
   pages, and how its tests run.

from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from to_weaviate.retry import with_retry


def test_with_retry_raises_permanent_error_at_once():
    calls = []

    def call():
        calls.append(1)
        raise ValueError("bad")

    sleeps: list[float] = []
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        with_retry(call, lambda exc: None, sleep=sleeps.append)
    assert len(calls) == 1 and sleeps == []


def test_with_retry_returns_after_transient_failures():
    results = [RuntimeError("a"), RuntimeError("b"), "ok"]

    def call():
        r = results.pop(0)
        if isinstance(r, Exception):
            raise r
        return r

    sleeps: list[float] = []
    assert with_retry(call, lambda exc: 0.0, sleep=sleeps.append) == "ok"
    assert len(sleeps) == 2


def test_with_retry_reraises_last_exception_after_all_attempts():
    errors = [RuntimeError(str(i)) for i in range(7)]
    sleeps: list[float] = []

    def call():
        raise errors.pop(0)

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="6"):
        with_retry(call, lambda exc: 0.0, sleep=sleeps.append)
    assert len(sleeps) == 6


def test_with_retry_delay_is_capped_at_30_seconds():
    sleeps: list[float] = []

    def call():
        raise RuntimeError("x")

    with patch("to_weaviate.retry.random.uniform", side_effect=lambda a, b: b):
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
            with_retry(call, lambda exc: 100.0, sleep=sleeps.append)
    assert sleeps == [30] * 6


def test_with_retry_backoff_grows_and_honors_minimum():
    sleeps: list[float] = []

    def call():
        raise RuntimeError("x")

    with patch("to_weaviate.retry.random.uniform", side_effect=lambda a, b: b):
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
            with_retry(call, lambda exc: 0.0, sleep=sleeps.append)
    assert sleeps == [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16]

    sleeps.clear()
    with patch("to_weaviate.retry.random.uniform", return_value=0.0):
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
            with_retry(call, lambda exc: 2.0, sleep=sleeps.append)
    assert sleeps == [2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0]


def test_a_full_retry_waits_at_least_15_seconds_and_at_most_31():
    def call():
        raise RuntimeError("x")

    for pick, expected in (
        (lambda a, b: a, [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8]),
        (lambda a, b: b, [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16]),
    ):
        sleeps: list[float] = []
        with patch("to_weaviate.retry.random.uniform", side_effect=pick):
            with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
                with_retry(call, lambda exc: 0.0, sleep=sleeps.append)
        assert sleeps == expected
    assert sum([0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8]) == 15.75
    assert sum([0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16]) == 31.5

# Both setups of the acceptance tests, with one call of acceptance.yml each.
# ci.yml and release.yml call this workflow.
name: acceptance suites

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read
  # The cluster setup pulls two images from private packages of this
  # repository.
  packages: read

jobs:
  single:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/acceptance.yml
    with: {name: single, replicas: 1, workers: 1, chroma: single}

  # The cluster setup pulls images from private packages. The token of a pull
  # request from a fork is not given access to them, so the setup does not
  # run there and cluster-not-run says so.
  cluster:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    uses: ./.github/workflows/acceptance.yml
    with: {name: cluster, replicas: 3, workers: 3, chroma: distributed}

  cluster-not-run:
    name: cluster (not run on a fork)
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: |
          message="The cluster suite did not run: this pull request comes from a fork, and the suite needs private images of the repository. A maintainer runs it by pushing the commits to a branch of weaviate/to-weaviate and running the ci workflow on that branch."
          echo "::warning::$message"
          echo "$message" >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Chroma images

# Builds Chroma's query-service and compactor-service without AVX-512 and
# pushes them to ghcr.io. Chroma publishes both images built with
# ENABLE_AVX512=1, and they stop with SIGILL on a runner whose CPU lacks
# avx512f. tests/acceptance/chroma-k8s.sh pins the images this workflow
# pushes. Run it once per Chroma version, then update the pins there. The
# packages stay private: only workflows of this repository pull them.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      chroma_version:
        description: Chroma release tag, for example 1.5.9
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

concurrency:
  group: chroma-images-${{ inputs.chroma_version }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CHROMA_VERSION: ${{ inputs.chroma_version }}
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io/weaviate/to-weaviate

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 240
    steps:
      - name: Check the version
        run: |
          if ! printf '%s' "$CHROMA_VERSION" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
            echo "::error::chroma_version must look like 1.5.9."
            exit 1
          fi
      # The release build of Chroma's Rust workspace needs more disk than a
      # runner has free.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
          docker system prune --all --force >/dev/null
          df -h /
      - name: Clone Chroma
        run: |
          git clone --quiet --depth 1 --branch "$CHROMA_VERSION" \
            https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma.git chroma
          echo "CHROMA_SHA=$(git -C chroma rev-parse HEAD)" >>"$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Log in to ghcr.io
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: printf '%s' "$GITHUB_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io --username "$GITHUB_ACTOR" --password-stdin
      # Both targets share the builder stage, so the second build compiles
      # nothing. ENABLE_AVX512 is left unset: the Dockerfile then adds no
      # AVX-512 compiler flag.
      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          : >digests.txt
          while read -r name target; do
            image="$REGISTRY/chroma-$name:$CHROMA_VERSION"
            if docker manifest inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::notice::$image exists. Not built again."
              docker pull --quiet "$image"
            else
              docker build chroma \
                --file chroma/rust/Dockerfile \
                --target "$target" \
                --build-arg RELEASE_MODE=1 \
                --label "org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
                --label "org.opencontainers.image.description=Chroma $name $CHROMA_VERSION built without AVX-512" \
                --label "org.opencontainers.image.revision=$CHROMA_SHA" \
                --tag "$image"
              docker push --quiet "$image"
            fi
            docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' "$image" >>digests.txt
          done <<'EOF'
          query-service query_service
          compactor-service compaction_service
          EOF
      - name: Report the digests
        run: |
          {
            echo "Chroma $CHROMA_VERSION, commit \`$CHROMA_SHA\`, built without AVX-512:"
            echo
            sed 's/^/- `/; s/$/`/' digests.txt
          } >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          cat digests.txt

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          # setuptools_scm reads the version from the tag.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # A release tag must point at a commit on main. With fetch-depth 0 the
      # checkout has origin/main; the fetch covers a checkout without it.
      - run: |
          git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/remotes/origin/main >/dev/null \
            || git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main; then
            echo "::error::$GITHUB_REF_NAME does not point at a commit on main."
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - run: pip install build==1.6.1
      - run: python -m build
      # The wheel version must be the tag without its v. Any other version
      # stops the release before the upload.
      - run: |
          wheel="dist/to_weaviate-${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}-py3-none-any.whl"
          if [ ! -f "$wheel" ]; then
            echo "::error::$wheel was not built. dist/ holds: $(ls dist | tr '\n' ' ')"
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
          if-no-files-found: error

  # The unit tests on the tagged commit, with the steps of the unit job in
  # ci.yml.
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.13", "3.14"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: uv sync --locked --extra test
      - run: uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit

  # Both acceptance suites on the tagged commit. packages: read is for the
  # private images of the cluster setup.
  acceptance:
    needs: build
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/acceptance-suites.yml

  # No always() here or in publish: a failed, cancelled or skipped job in
  # needs skips the job, so nothing is released without the unit tests and
  # both suites.
  github-release:
    needs: [build, unit, acceptance]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
      # The release carries the wheel and the sdist, the exact files of the
      # version; their dependencies still come from PyPI. A release that
      # exists (made by hand, or a rerun) gets the files instead of an error.
      # --verify-tag refuses to create the tag.
      - run: |
          if gh release view "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" dist/* --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" dist/* --verify-tag --generate-notes
          fi
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

  # Runs last: a PyPI version cannot be replaced, a GitHub release can.
  publish:
    needs: [unit, acceptance, github-release]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    environment: pypi
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@7245906fb61fa33a13554f9d5fb856fe61758086 # v1.14.3

# Testing

The tests check that a migration loses no record, writes none twice, leaks
no secret, resumes after a killed process or a refused write, and reports
each failure with the right exit code. They run at three levels.

| Level | Where | Servers | Runs in CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | `tests/unit/` | None. Fakes stand in for the source and Weaviate. | Yes, on Python 3.10, 3.13 and 3.14 |
| Acceptance, API | `tests/acceptance/` | A real source and a real Weaviate, reached only through the `to-weaviate` command and the server APIs | On pull requests and releases |
| Acceptance, infra | `tests/acceptance/`, marker `infra` | Also restarts or deletes a server through Docker or kubectl | On pull requests and releases |

The API level also runs against a Weaviate Cloud cluster with
`make acceptance-cloud`, by hand before a release. See
[Against Weaviate Cloud](#against-weaviate-cloud).

Acceptance tests exist for Chroma only, in `tests/acceptance/chroma/`. Each
new source adds its own directory, `tests/acceptance/<name>/`. The shared
pieces are `tests/acceptance/conftest.py` and `tests/e2e.py`.

## What the tests cover

| Area | What the tests check |
|---|---|
| Lost or duplicated records | Faults in the middle of a page, short pages, refused batches, objects above the gRPC message limit, two source ids with one UUID, a second `copy` on the same directory, a 50,000-record copy |
| Resuming | A killed `copy`, a refused page, a refused quantizer update, a state file of an older or newer format, a corrupted state file, a changed target or source |
| Sync | Records added, changed and deleted after the copy, `--prune` and its 10% limit, a source written to during the id listing, one tenant of a shared collection with an object the tool did not write, a plan edit after the copy, rejects written once the plan is fixed |
| Secrets | No API key, URL password or embedding-function secret in any output, traceback or file of the migration directory. The acceptance suite checks stdout and stderr of each command that it runs to completion, and every file under the test's directory. A command started in the background (`start` in `tests/e2e.py`) has its stderr discarded. |
| Plan and schema | Every plan field, the allowed edits end to end, the index and quantizer rules, property types and conversions, names that need renaming, existing collections with other settings |
| Data fidelity | Distances, metadata types, values at the type limits, unicode, empty and long values, embedding-function mappings |
| Exit codes and JSON | Every error code and its exit code, one JSON document on stdout, text mode |
| Faults on a 3-node cluster | A Weaviate pod deleted during `copy` and during `verify`, each consistency level on 3 replicas |
| Source behavior | For Chroma: the page order, a Chroma restart during a copy, and a copy while distributed Chroma compacts |

## Not covered

- Chroma Cloud. No test account exists. The unit tests cover the tool's side
  with fakes, and the `cluster` setup of CI covers distributed
  Chroma, which Chroma Cloud runs. Its quotas, rate limits and sharded
  collections stay untested.
- A Weaviate Cloud sandbox cluster, and Weaviate versions other than
  `tests/acceptance/weaviate-version`.
- A Weaviate key that may read but not write. Unit tests cover the error.
- Faults that need a proxy: a connection reset inside a response body, or a
  server slow enough to hit a timeout. Unit tests inject them.
- Values that Chroma refuses to store, such as vectors of mixed dimension or
  ints outside int64. Unit tests cover the tool's side.
- Vectorizers that call a model provider. CI has no provider keys.
- Windows, Ctrl-C, and sources of millions of records.

## Unit tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit
```

`tests/unit/fakes.py` holds `FakeSource` and the fake Weaviate writer, reader
and schema. `tests/unit/chroma_server.py` serves a fake Chroma through
`httpx.MockTransport`, so the CLI tests run the real Chroma client.

## Acceptance tests

The acceptance tests run the installed `to-weaviate` command against real
servers that are already running. No test starts a server. Some `infra`
tests restart the compose Chroma or delete a Weaviate pod. The tests run
only against the test endpoints:

```bash
WEAVIATE_URL=http://localhost:8099
WEAVIATE_GRPC_URL=http://localhost:50099
WEAVIATE_API_KEY=admin-key
CHROMA_URL=http://localhost:8001
```

When a variable is missing or has another value, the suite skips every test
and names the variable. With `TO_WEAVIATE_REQUIRE_ACCEPTANCE=1`, as in CI,
it fails instead. It connects to no server before this check passes. The
commands it runs get empty `CHROMA_DATABASE`, `CHROMA_TENANT`,
`CHROMA_API_KEY` and `CHROMA_TOKEN_HEADER`, so values from your shell do not
reach them.

The suite deletes and recreates the Chroma collections that `seed.py`
creates. Before and after each test it deletes the Weaviate collections in
`SUITE_COLLECTIONS` (`tests/acceptance/conftest.py`), and it writes to no
other collection.

`pytest -m "not infra"` runs the API level only.

### With Docker

```bash
make chroma-up       # Chroma on port 8001
make weaviate-up     # Weaviate and text2vec-transformers on ports 8099 and 50099
source .venv/bin/activate
WEAVIATE_ASYNC_INDEXING=true make acceptance
make weaviate-down
make chroma-down
```

`make weaviate-up` starts Weaviate with `ASYNC_INDEXING=true`, as Weaviate
Cloud runs. `ASYNC=0 make weaviate-up` starts it without; then run the suite
with `WEAVIATE_ASYNC_INDEXING=false make acceptance`. A few tests depend on
async indexing and read this variable.

### With a kind cluster

`make acceptance-up` starts Chroma and a Weaviate kind cluster named
`weaviate-k8s` through a clone of
[weaviate-local-k8s](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate-local-k8s) at
`LOCAL_K8S` (default: `../weaviate-local-k8s`). It needs Docker, `kind`,
`helm`, `kubectl`, `curl`, `jq`, `lsof`, `nohup`, and `gtimeout` on macOS or
`timeout` on Linux. It stops when a kind cluster with that name exists, and
it switches the kubectl context to `kind-weaviate-k8s`.

```bash
make acceptance-up
source .venv/bin/activate
make acceptance
make acceptance-down   # stops Chroma, then asks before it deletes the cluster
```

`make acceptance-down` deletes only the cluster that `make acceptance-up`
created, and only after you type `y`. The cleanup of weaviate-local-k8s also
kills every `kubectl-relay` process on the machine and leaves no kubectl
context selected.

### Against Weaviate Cloud

`make acceptance-cloud` runs the API level against a Weaviate Cloud cluster,
with the local test Chroma as the source. Use a dedicated serverless
cluster: the suite fails before its first test when the cluster holds a
collection outside `SUITE_COLLECTIONS`. The cluster must have
`text2vec-weaviate` enabled and at least one of the `CANDIDATE_MODULES` of
`tests/acceptance/chroma/test_check.py` disabled.

Put the two `export` lines in a file outside the repository, so the key stays
out of your shell history, and `source` it:

```bash
make chroma-up
source ~/weaviate-cloud-test.sh   # export WEAVIATE_URL=... and export WEAVIATE_API_KEY=...
source .venv/bin/activate
make acceptance-cloud
```

Do not set the two variables on the `make` command line. Make passes such
values to every child process, and the target refuses them.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs these jobs:

| Job | What it runs | Pull request | Push to `main` | Manual run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lint` | `pre-commit run --all-files`: ruff, ruff-format, mypy | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `unit` | `pytest tests/unit` on Python 3.10, 3.13 and 3.14 | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `unit (lowest deps)` | `pytest tests/unit` on Python 3.10 with the lower bound of each dependency in `pyproject.toml` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `acceptance` | Both acceptance setups, through `.github/workflows/acceptance-suites.yml` | Yes | No | Yes |

A manual run is "Run workflow" on the CI workflow page, or
`gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>`. `.github/workflows/release.yml`
runs the `unit` and the `acceptance` job on the tagged commit. See [Releasing](releasing.md).

Every job except `unit (lowest deps)` installs the versions in `uv.lock` with
`uv sync --locked --extra test`, which fails when `uv.lock` does not match
`pyproject.toml`. The mypy hook is the exception inside `lint`: pre-commit
installs the packages in `additional_dependencies` of
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`, not the versions in `uv.lock`. Those entries carry
the bounds of `pyproject.toml`.

The `acceptance` job has two setups. Each runs Weaviate in a kind cluster
with `ASYNC_INDEXING`.

| Setup | Servers | Check that holds its result |
|---|---|---|
| `single` | One Weaviate node and the single-node Chroma | `acceptance / single / run` |
| `cluster` | Three Weaviate nodes with replication factor 3 and distributed Chroma | `acceptance / cluster / run` |

The tests in `tests/acceptance/chroma/test_cluster.py` run in the `cluster`
setup only. Each setup uploads its JUnit XML as the artifact
`acceptance-junit-single` or `acceptance-junit-cluster`.
`test_copy_during_compaction` records its measurements there as test
properties.

### The images of the cluster setup

Chroma publishes its `query-service` and `compactor-service` images built
with AVX-512. Part of GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners have a CPU without it,
and both services exit with SIGILL there. The `cluster` setup uses builds of
the same Chroma release without AVX-512, from two private packages of the
repository: `chroma-query-service` and `chroma-compactor-service`.
`tests/acceptance/chroma-k8s.sh` pins each by its digest.

To move to another Chroma release, run the `Chroma images` workflow with the
release tag. It takes about an hour. Its summary lists the two digests. Set
`CHROMA_TAG`, `CHROMA_COMMIT` and the two digests in `chroma-k8s.sh`.

A pull request from a fork cannot read the packages, so the `cluster` setup
does not run there. The check `acceptance / cluster (not run on a fork)`
says so with a warning. Before the merge, push the commits to a branch of
`weaviate/to-weaviate` and run the `ci` workflow on it:

```bash
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>
```

## Writing tests

- A behavior change comes with a unit test that fails without it.
- An acceptance test reaches the servers only through the command and the
  server APIs, unless it needs to restart or delete a server. Then it
  carries the `infra` marker.
- Test data for a source lives in its `seed.py`. A new target collection
  goes into `SUITE_COLLECTIONS`, so the suite cleans it up.
- Use made-up keys in tests, never real ones.

# One setup of the acceptance tests: Weaviate in a kind cluster through the
# weaviate-local-k8s action, a Chroma, and the suite under tests/acceptance.
# acceptance-suites.yml calls it once per setup.
name: acceptance

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      name:
        description: The name of the setup, single or cluster.
        required: true
        type: string
      replicas:
        description: Weaviate pods. The cases of test_cluster.py run when it is at least 3.
        required: true
        type: number
      workers:
        description: Worker nodes of the kind cluster.
        required: true
        type: number
      chroma:
        description: >-
          The Chroma of the setup. single is the compose container; distributed
          is the open-source distributed Chroma in the kind cluster, with
          which the seed waits for compaction and the compaction case of
          test_source_order.py runs.
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read
  # The cluster setup pulls two images from private packages of this
  # repository.
  packages: read

jobs:
  tests:
    name: run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      WEAVIATE_URL: http://localhost:8099
      WEAVIATE_GRPC_URL: http://localhost:50099
      WEAVIATE_API_KEY: admin-key
      CHROMA_URL: http://localhost:8001
      TO_WEAVIATE_REQUIRE_ACCEPTANCE: "1"
      # Every Weaviate Cloud instance runs with ASYNC_INDEXING, so both setups
      # do. Read by the tests whose outcome depends on it.
      WEAVIATE_ASYNC_INDEXING: "true"
      ACCEPTANCE_NODES: ${{ inputs.replicas }}
      ACCEPTANCE_CHROMA: ${{ inputs.chroma }}
    steps:
      # Chroma's own query-service and compactor-service images exit with
      # SIGILL on a CPU without AVX-512, which part of the ubuntu-latest pool
      # lacks. chroma-k8s.sh pins builds without it. The line shows which CPU
      # a run of the cluster setup had.
      - if: inputs.chroma == 'distributed'
        run: |
          model=$(sed -n 's/^model name[[:space:]]*: //p' /proc/cpuinfo | head -n 1)
          if grep -q -w avx512f /proc/cpuinfo; then flag=with; else flag=without; fi
          echo "The runner's CPU is $model, $flag avx512f."
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
      - run: echo "WEAVIATE_VERSION=$(cat tests/acceptance/weaviate-version)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # The action runs its own checkout, so it comes before any step that
      # writes to the workspace.
      - uses: weaviate/weaviate-local-k8s@d05542c6414333ad1011a5e7341b03a210754648 # v2
        with:
          weaviate-version: ${{ env.WEAVIATE_VERSION }}
          workers: ${{ inputs.workers }}
          replicas: ${{ inputs.replicas }}
          weaviate-port: 8099
          weaviate-grpc-port: 50099
          rbac: true
          modules: text2vec-transformers
          expose-pods: false
          # The chart passes each env entry to the Weaviate pods.
          values-override: |
            env:
              ASYNC_INDEXING: "true"
      # The kubectl-relay forwards of the action can stop forwarding gRPC
      # after the SIGKILL resume test; the script replaces them.
      - id: forward
        run: sh tests/acceptance/port-forward.sh
      - if: inputs.chroma == 'single'
        run: docker compose -f tests/acceptance/chroma/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait
      # chroma-k8s.sh pulls its two private images with this login.
      - if: inputs.chroma == 'distributed'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: printf '%s' "$GITHUB_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io --username "$GITHUB_ACTOR" --password-stdin
      # Deploys distributed Chroma in the kind cluster and forwards its
      # frontend to port 8001.
      - if: inputs.chroma == 'distributed'
        run: sh tests/acceptance/chroma-k8s.sh up
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with: {python-version: "3.13"}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with: {python-version: "3.13"}
      - run: uv sync --locked --extra test && uv run --no-sync pytest tests/acceptance -v --junitxml=/tmp/acceptance-junit.xml
      # A case can record measurements as test properties, which only the XML
      # holds on a pass.
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: acceptance-junit-${{ inputs.name }}
          path: /tmp/acceptance-junit.xml
      # Each forward's log has a line for each start and exit of its kubectl
      # port-forward, so this step shows whether a forward died during the
      # suite and when; the gRPC forward of the action died after
      # test_resume.py killed a copy. The cluster setup also has the log of the
      # Chroma forward. A failure prints the full tails, for a test that
      # failed with exit 4.
      - if: always() && steps.forward.outcome == 'success'
        run: grep -E 'starting|exited|lost connection' /tmp/port-forward-*.log | tail -n 100
      - if: failure()
        run: tail -n 200 /tmp/port-forward-*.log
      # The restart counts, the compactor pod (an OOM kill shows there), and
      # the last log lines of each pod of five Chroma services; the previous
      # log too for a pod that restarted. The label app of each workload is
      # its name in the chart, so sts/query-service gives both of its pods.
      - if: failure() && inputs.chroma == 'distributed'
        run: |
          kubectl -n chroma get pods -o wide || true
          kubectl -n chroma describe pod -l app=compaction-service || true
          for workload in sts/compaction-service sts/rust-log-service \
            deploy/rust-frontend-service sts/query-service deploy/sysdb; do
            for pod in $(kubectl -n chroma get pods -l "app=${workload#*/}" -o name || true); do
              echo "--- $workload: kubectl -n chroma logs $pod --tail=500"
              kubectl -n chroma logs "$pod" --all-containers --tail=500 || true
              restarts=$(kubectl -n chroma get "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}' || true)
              if [ "${restarts:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
                echo "--- $workload: kubectl -n chroma logs $pod --previous --tail=500 ($restarts restarts)"
                kubectl -n chroma logs "$pod" --all-containers --previous --tail=500 || true
              fi
            done
          done

"""Create and change the Chroma collection `support-articles` of the README demo.

Usage:
  python docs/demo/seed.py [COUNT]   create the collection with COUNT records
  python docs/demo/seed.py change    change it, as an application would after
                                     the copy: add 5 records, update 5, delete 5

Reads CHROMA_URL (default http://localhost:8001) and refuses any host other
than localhost, because it deletes the collection first. Each record has a
document, four scalar metadata keys and a 1536-dimension unit vector, the
size of OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small. The vectors are random, with a
fixed seed, so every run creates the same collection.
"""

import math
import os
import random
import sys
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import httpx

NAME = "support-articles"
DIMENSION = 1536
BATCH = 300
DATABASE_PATH = "/api/v2/tenants/default_tenant/databases/default_database"
DEFAULT_COUNT = 5000
# `change` adds the records numbered from DEFAULT_COUNT, updates the document
# of the first CHANGED records and deletes the CHANGED records after those.
CHANGED = 5

PRODUCTS = [
    "Billing",
    "Dashboards",
    "Exports",
    "Alerts",
    "Single sign-on",
    "Mobile app",
]
TASKS = [
    "set up {p} for a new team",
    "fix a {p} error after an upgrade",
    "move {p} settings between workspaces",
    "limit who can change {p}",
    "audit recent changes to {p}",
    "connect {p} to an external tool",
]
DETAILS = [
    "The steps apply to every plan.",
    "An administrator role is required.",
    "Changes take effect within five minutes.",
    "The old settings stay available for 30 days.",
    "Each workspace keeps its own copy.",
]


def unit_vector(rng: random.Random) -> list[float]:
    values = [rng.gauss(0.0, 1.0) for _ in range(DIMENSION)]
    norm = math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in values))
    return [round(v / norm, 6) for v in values]


def records(count: int) -> list[dict]:
    rng = random.Random(7)
    out = []
    for i in range(count):
        product = PRODUCTS[i % len(PRODUCTS)]
        task = TASKS[(i // len(PRODUCTS)) % len(TASKS)].format(p=product.lower())
        out.append(
            {
                "id": f"kb-{i:05d}",
                "document": f"How to {task}. {rng.choice(DETAILS)}",
                "metadata": {
                    "product": product,
                    "year": 2019 + i % 7,
                    "views": rng.randint(10, 50_000),
                    "verified": i % 3 != 0,
                },
                "embedding": unit_vector(rng),
            }
        )
    return out


def _url() -> str:
    url = os.environ.get("CHROMA_URL", "http://localhost:8001")
    if urlsplit(url).hostname not in ("localhost", "127.0.0.1"):
        sys.exit(
            f"seed.py changes {NAME}, so it runs only against localhost, not {url}"
        )
    return url


def _client() -> httpx.Client:
    return httpx.Client(base_url=_url() + DATABASE_PATH, timeout=60)


def _add(http: httpx.Client, collection_id: str, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    for start in range(0, len(rows), BATCH):
        batch = rows[start : start + BATCH]
        added = http.post(
            f"/collections/{collection_id}/add",
            json={
                key + "s": [r[key] for r in batch]
                for key in ("id", "document", "metadata", "embedding")
            },
        )
        added.raise_for_status()


def create(count: int) -> None:
    with _client() as http:
        deleted = http.delete(f"/collections/{NAME}")
        if deleted.status_code != 404:
            deleted.raise_for_status()
        created = http.post(
            "/collections",
            json={"name": NAME, "configuration": {"hnsw": {"space": "cosine"}}},
        )
        created.raise_for_status()
        _add(http, created.json()["id"], records(count))
    print(f"Created {NAME} with {count} records of dimension {DIMENSION} at {_url()}")


def change() -> None:
    """Add CHANGED records, update the documents of CHANGED and delete CHANGED."""
    rows = records(DEFAULT_COUNT + CHANGED)
    updated = rows[:CHANGED]
    removed = rows[CHANGED : 2 * CHANGED]
    with _client() as http:
        found = http.get(f"/collections/{NAME}")
        found.raise_for_status()
        collection_id = found.json()["id"]
        _add(http, collection_id, rows[DEFAULT_COUNT:])
        changed = http.post(
            f"/collections/{collection_id}/update",
            json={
                "ids": [r["id"] for r in updated],
                "documents": ["Updated: " + r["document"] for r in updated],
            },
        )
        changed.raise_for_status()
        deleted = http.post(
            f"/collections/{collection_id}/delete",
            json={"ids": [r["id"] for r in removed]},
        )
        deleted.raise_for_status()
    print(
        f"Changed {NAME}: added {CHANGED} records, updated {CHANGED}, deleted {CHANGED}"
    )


def main() -> None:
    if sys.argv[1:] == ["change"]:
        change()
    else:
        create(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else DEFAULT_COUNT)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# to-weaviate

[![CI](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: BSD-3-Clause](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BSD--3--Clause-blue.svg)](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/pyproject.toml)

`to-weaviate` migrates collections from another vector database into
[Weaviate](https://weaviate.io).

> [!NOTE]
> Chroma is the only supported source. To ask for another one,
> [open an issue](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/issues/new).

![to-weaviate inspect reads a Chroma collection of 5,000 records with 1536-dimension vectors, the start of plan.yaml shows the source and target, then check and copy run, sync --prune writes the 10 records that changed since the copy and deletes the 5 whose source record is gone, and verify prints PASS for the count, ids and records checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/main/docs/demo/demo.gif)

The Weaviate team maintains it.

## Supported sources

| Source | Deployments | Inspect command | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chroma | Chroma Cloud, distributed Chroma, single-node Chroma, a Chroma directory on disk | `inspect chroma` | [Chroma](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/sources/chroma.md) |

## Features

- **Read-only on the source.** No command writes to it or deletes from it.
- **A plan you review first.** `inspect` drafts `plan.yaml`; nothing reaches
  Weaviate until you run `copy` or `sync`.
- **Safe to rerun.** A rerun of `copy` continues at the page where the last
  run stopped. Each object's UUID comes from its source id, so a rerun
  writes no duplicate.
- **Verified.** `verify` compares counts, ids, and a sample of records with
  their vectors, and writes a report.
- **No secrets in output.** Keys come from the environment, and no output or
  file holds one.

## Requirements & Installation

- Python 3.10 or newer.
- A Weaviate instance: a [Weaviate Cloud](https://console.weaviate.cloud)
  cluster, or a [server you run yourself](https://docs.weaviate.io/deploy).
  A free (sandbox) Weaviate Cloud cluster accepts only the index type
  `hfresh`; for one, run `inspect` with `--index hfresh`.
  [Weaviate target](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/weaviate.md) has the details.
  The server must run Weaviate 1.27.0 or later; see
  [Supported Weaviate versions](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/weaviate.md#supported-weaviate-versions).
- Read access to the source. See the [source guide](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/sources/README.md).

```bash
pip install to-weaviate
```

To run it without installing, use [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
uvx to-weaviate --help
```

Each [GitHub release](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/releases) also
carries the wheel and the sdist of that version.

## Migration steps

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    inspect["inspect #60;source#62;"] --> review["review plan.yaml"] --> check --> copy --> sync["sync --prune"] --> verify
    copy -. "run again to resume" .-> copy
```

1. Run `to-weaviate inspect <source>`. It reads the source and writes a
   draft `plan.yaml`.
2. Review the plan. Edit the names, types or vector settings you want to
   change.
3. Run `to-weaviate check`. It validates the plan against Weaviate and
   creates nothing.
4. Run `to-weaviate copy`. It creates the collections and copies the
   records. If it stops, run it again to resume. Some sources need the
   writes to them paused while `copy` and `sync` run; the "Writes during a
   copy" section of each [source guide](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/sources/README.md) says which.
5. Optional: run `to-weaviate sync` to write the records that are new or
   changed since the copy. Run it as often as you like before the last step.
6. Stop the writes to the source, then run `to-weaviate sync --prune`. It
   writes the records that are new or changed since the last run and
   deletes the objects whose source record is gone.
7. Run `to-weaviate verify`. It compares Weaviate with the source and writes
   `report.md`. When every check passes, switch your application to
   Weaviate.

Run `to-weaviate status` at any time to see the copy progress. It needs no
credentials. Every command uses one migration directory, `./.to-weaviate`
unless you pass `--dir`.

## Example

This example migrates one collection from Chroma Cloud to Weaviate Cloud.
It assumes:

- The Chroma Cloud collection is `support-articles`: 5,000 records with
  1536-dimension vectors.
- The Weaviate Cloud cluster is not a free (sandbox) cluster.
- The application does not write to the collection while `copy` and `sync`
  run. Chroma Cloud needs that.
- You run every command in one directory, and the settings are in a `.env`
  file there or exported.

For a server you run yourself, the [Chroma guide](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/sources/chroma.md)
and [Weaviate target](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/weaviate.md) list the settings.

### Configure

```dotenv
CHROMA_API_KEY=<Chroma Cloud API key>
WEAVIATE_URL=https://my-cluster.weaviate.cloud
WEAVIATE_API_KEY=<Weaviate API key>
```

`WEAVIATE_URL` and `WEAVIATE_API_KEY` are the URL and an API key of the
Weaviate Cloud cluster. Both are in the
[Weaviate Cloud console](https://console.weaviate.cloud). `CHROMA_API_KEY`
is a Chroma Cloud API key. The [Chroma guide](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/sources/chroma.md) lists
the other Chroma settings.

### Inspect and review the plan

```console
$ to-weaviate inspect chroma --collection support-articles
Inspecting Chroma at https://api.trychroma.com
support-articles -> Support_articles
  count: 5000
  dimension: 1536
  distance: cosine
  vectors: default (keep, no vectorizer)
Decisions:
  support-articles (vector_mode): No Weaviate vectorizer matches the source embedding function. Either supply query vectors from the application, or run inspect with --vectors embed to re-vectorize the documents in Weaviate.
Review .to-weaviate/plan.yaml, then run to-weaviate check.
```

Each entry of `.to-weaviate/plan.yaml` maps one source collection to one
Weaviate collection. An excerpt:

```yaml
collections:
- source:
    name: support-articles
    count: 5000
    dimension: 1536
  target:
    name: Support_articles
    vectors:
    - name: default
      mode: keep
      distance: cosine
    properties:
    - source_key: product
      name: product
      type: text
    - source_key: views
      name: views
      type: int
    - source_key: verified
      name: verified
      type: boolean
```

[The plan file](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/plan-file.md) lists the edits you can make.

### Check and copy

```console
$ to-weaviate check
Checking the target at https://my-cluster.weaviate.cloud
No errors, 0 warnings.

$ to-weaviate copy
Copying support-articles to Support_articles
Copied support-articles: 5000 records, 0 rejects
support-articles -> Support_articles: copied 5000 of 5000, rejects 0, done
Total: 5000 records
```

### Sync, verify and switch

Stop the writes to the source. Here the source gained 5 records, 5 changed
and 5 were deleted after the copy:

```console
$ to-weaviate sync --prune
Syncing support-articles to Support_articles
Synced support-articles to Support_articles: 10 records written, 4990 unchanged, 0 rejects, 5 stale, 5 deleted
support-articles -> Support_articles: copied 10, unchanged 4990, rejects 0, stale 5, deleted 5
Total: copied 10, unchanged 4990, rejects 0, stale 5, deleted 5

$ to-weaviate verify
Verifying support-articles in Support_articles
PASS Support_articles count: source count 5000, target count 5000
PASS Support_articles ids: missing 0, extra 0
PASS Support_articles records: sampled 300, compared 300, rejects skipped 0, differing 0
```

Now switch your application to Weaviate. Do not run `sync` against this
target afterwards: the source no longer holds the current data.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `inspect <source>` | Reads the source collections and writes `inspect.json` and a draft `plan.yaml`. |
| `check` | Validates `plan.yaml` against Weaviate: names, types, vectorizer modules, provider keys, existing collections. Creates nothing. |
| `copy` | Creates the collections and copies the records. Run it again to resume or to copy new records. |
| `sync` | Writes the records that are new or changed since the copy. With `--prune`, deletes the objects whose source record is gone. |
| `verify` | Compares counts, ids and a sample of records, and writes `report.md` and `report.json`. |
| `status` | Shows the progress of each collection from the migration directory. |

Every command takes `--dir` and `--json`. With `--json`, stdout holds one
JSON document. The exit code names the class of failure, with and without
`--json`:

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | Rejected records, a failed verification, or stale objects above 10% that `sync --prune` left alone |
| 2 | A usage, plan, state or directory error, a request the source refused, or an unconfirmed first run into a collection that holds objects `sync --prune` would delete |
| 3 | A missing or refused credential |
| 4 | An unreachable server, a source that is compacting or still written to, or a deletion Weaviate did only partly |
| 5 | An internal error |

[Commands](https://github.com/weaviate/to-weaviate/blob/main/docs/commands.md#exit-codes) lists every error code.

"""The mypy hook installs its own packages, apart from uv.lock."""

import re
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

# mypy reads types-PyYAML instead of pyyaml.
STUBBED = {"pyyaml"}


def _project_dependencies() -> list[str]:
    text = (ROOT / "pyproject.toml").read_text()
    block = re.search(r"^dependencies = \[\n(.*?)^\]", text, re.M | re.S)
    assert block is not None
    return re.findall(r'^\s*"([^"]+)",?\s*$', block.group(1), re.M)


def _mypy_hook_dependencies() -> list[str]:
    config = yaml.safe_load((ROOT / ".pre-commit-config.yaml").read_text())
    hooks = [hook for repo in config["repos"] for hook in repo["hooks"]]
    (mypy,) = [hook for hook in hooks if hook["id"] == "mypy"]
    return list(mypy["additional_dependencies"])


def test_mypy_hook_uses_the_bounds_of_pyproject() -> None:
    dependencies = _project_dependencies()
    assert len(dependencies) == 6
    expected = [d for d in dependencies if re.split(r"[<>=]", d)[0] not in STUBBED]
    hook = _mypy_hook_dependencies()
    assert [d for d in expected if d not in hook] == []

import json

import pytest

from to_weaviate.events import Events


class FakeClock:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.now = 0.0

    def __call__(self) -> float:
        return self.now


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _close_events(monkeypatch):
    opened: list[Events] = []
    original = Events.__init__

    def init(self, *args, **kwargs):
        original(self, *args, **kwargs)
        opened.append(self)

    monkeypatch.setattr(Events, "__init__", init)
    yield
    for ev in opened:
        ev.close()


def read(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines()]


def test_progress_events_are_throttled(tmp_path):
    clock = FakeClock()
    ev = Events(tmp_path / "events.jsonl", clock)
    for i in range(1000):
        ev.progress("c1", i, 1000)
    assert len((tmp_path / "events.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()) == 1


def test_progress_writes_again_after_five_seconds(tmp_path):
    clock = FakeClock()
    ev = Events(tmp_path / "events.jsonl", clock)
    ev.progress("c1", 1, 10)
    clock.now = 4.9
    ev.progress("c1", 2, 10)
    clock.now = 5.0
    ev.progress("c1", 3, 10)
    assert [e["copied"] for e in read(tmp_path / "events.jsonl")] == [1, 3]


def test_progress_throttle_is_per_ref(tmp_path):
    ev = Events(tmp_path / "events.jsonl", FakeClock())
    ev.progress("c1", 1, 10)
    ev.progress("c2", 1, 10)
    assert [e["ref"] for e in read(tmp_path / "events.jsonl")] == ["c1", "c2"]


def test_emit_line_shape_and_parent_dir(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "nested" / "events.jsonl"
    ev = Events(path)
    ev.emit("info", "started", ref="c1", count=3)
    [line] = read(path)
    assert line["level"] == "info"
    assert line["event"] == "started"
    assert line["ref"] == "c1"
    assert line["count"] == 3
    assert line["ts"].endswith("+00:00")


def test_progress_line_fields(tmp_path):
    ev = Events(tmp_path / "events.jsonl", FakeClock())
    ev.progress("c1", 5, 10)
    [line] = read(tmp_path / "events.jsonl")
    assert (line["event"], line["ref"], line["copied"], line["total"]) == (
        "progress",
        "c1",
        5,
        10,
    )

    ev.emit("info", "x")
    ev.progress("c1", 1, 2)
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert captured.out == "" and captured.err == ""

import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

from to_weaviate.lock import Locked, exclusive_lock

HOLDER = """
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from to_weaviate.lock import exclusive_lock

with exclusive_lock(Path(sys.argv[1])):
    print("held", flush=True)
    time.sleep(60)
"""

WITHOUT_FCNTL = """
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.modules["fcntl"] = None  # import fcntl now raises ImportError
from to_weaviate.lock import exclusive_lock

path = Path(sys.argv[1])
with exclusive_lock(path), exclusive_lock(path):
    print("ran")
"""


def test_a_second_lock_is_refused_until_the_first_ends(tmp_path):
    pytest.importorskip("fcntl")
    path = tmp_path / "copy.lock"
    with exclusive_lock(path):
        with pytest.raises(Locked), exclusive_lock(path):
            pass
    with exclusive_lock(path):
        pass
    assert path.exists()


def test_an_existing_unlocked_file_does_not_block(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "copy.lock"
    path.write_text("")
    with exclusive_lock(path):
        pass


def test_a_killed_holder_leaves_no_lock(tmp_path):
    pytest.importorskip("fcntl")
    path = tmp_path / "copy.lock"
    with subprocess.Popen(
        [sys.executable, "-c", HOLDER, str(path)], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True
    ) as holder:
        try:
            assert holder.stdout is not None
            assert holder.stdout.readline() == "held\n"
            with pytest.raises(Locked), exclusive_lock(path):
                pass
        finally:
            holder.kill()
    with exclusive_lock(path):
        pass


def test_without_fcntl_the_module_imports_and_runs_without_a_lock(tmp_path):
    done = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", WITHOUT_FCNTL, str(tmp_path / "copy.lock")],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=60,
        check=False,
    )
    assert (done.returncode, done.stdout) == (0, "ran\n"), done.stderr
